claims.evidence: Photo 0 confirms Sigma 12-24mm branding and focal range, but no mount/contacts shot to confirm Canon EF fit; 'US used' origin is unverifiable from photos.

risks.if_unproven: priced as mount-unconfirmed, worst case assuming it may not fit the buyer's Canon body

risks.risk: Internal fungus, haze, or oil on aperture blades not visible in current photos
risks.proof: A photo with a flashlight shone through the lens at an angle, and a photo of the rear element
risks.if_unproven: priced as not confirmed clean, i.e. as if fungus/haze may be present

risks.risk: Autofocus motor or aperture ring may not function despite 'perfect condition' claim
risks.proof: A short video showing autofocus engaging on a camera body and the aperture blades stopping down

risks.risk: Mismatch between seller's boilerplate text (shutter count, battery/charger) and actual item suggests the description was copied from another listing, reducing trust in all unverified claims
risks.proof: A fresh, item-specific description or photos matching the actual lens (e.g., box, caps, lens hood together)
risks.if_unproven: treat all unverified claims as unproven, not as evidence of condition

proof_requests: Photo of the rear lens mount showing electrical contacts to confirm Canon EF fit
Video of autofocus and aperture operation when mounted on a camera
Photo of the rear element and a flashlight-through shot to check for fungus/haze
Photo of included accessories (caps, hood, pouch) actually belonging to this lens
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a Sigma 12-24mm lens from the visible branding and focal markings, but working condition, mount fit, and internal cleanliness are unverified, and several seller claims don't even apply to a lens, so it must be priced at worst case using the cheapest generic lens comparable and capped near the lower Canon-lens comparable rather than higher-spec items.
